messages:
alex: Heads-up — I ran the streaming vs non-streaming replay this morning and saw a ~18% tail-latency regression for streaming on the same model. Trying to figure out whether it's kernel selection, batching heuristics, or KV cache behavior.
maria: did you use the same client chunking settings for both runs? small chunks add perf overhead.
alex: yes — same chunk_size=512 bytes + same decode args. harness command: `./tools/replay.sh --trace traces/2026-03-15.replay --mode=streaming --concurrency=16 --rps=120` and then `--mode=nonstreaming` for the other run.
henry: can you paste the perf profile output? specifically kernel selection stats (cuda kernels chosen) and batch size distribution.
alex: attaching snippets from the runtime profiler:
```
SUMMARY:
model: redwood-v2-small
runtime kernel: flash_attn_v2 (84% requests), fallback_f32 (16%)
batch size p50/p95/p99 = 1/4/8
kv_cache hit rate: 0.62
streaming chunk overhead: avg 3.2ms per chunk
```
nat: 0.62 KV hit is suspiciously low for replays — are you replaying short-turn chat traces or multi-turn? low KV hit increases memory reads and kernel fallback.
alex: these traces are multi-turn (avg context 1200 tokens) but the replay harness strips client-side incremental inputs to force streaming small deltas — intended.
emily: two quick hypotheses: 1) streaming adds small per-chunk work (serialize+send+io) which prevents larger batching and causes more fallback kernels; 2) our kernel selector thresholds prefer the optimized kernel only above some sequence length or batch size.
lucas: also check the batching heuristic: if continuous batching has a max-wait of 2ms, streaming client's frequent small chunks might flush early and produce tiny batches.
alex: agreed. here's the exact runtime config used for both runs:
```
--batch.max_wait_ms=2
--batch.max_size=16
--kernel.select_policy=latency_pref
--kv.cache_mode=on
--io.chunk_size=512
```
maria: can you rerun with `--batch.max_wait_ms=10` to let more requests coalesce? that should show whether batching is the main culprit.
alex: running now. also going to force kernel selection to `throughput_pref` to see kernel switches.
replay-bot: Job 37892 started: replay 1762501234 (streaming -> batch_wait=10) queued on eng-runtime-perf
henry: while that runs, please capture the client read-loop timings. If the client isn't aggressively consuming, backpressure could cause extra queuing inside runtime and different kernel paths.
alex: good call — added `--client.read_loop_profile=true` to the run.
replay-bot: Job 37892 completed: 1200 requests processed. Results uploaded to /tmp/replays/1762501234-streaming-10ms.json
alex: new numbers: p99 latency down from 320ms to 260ms, KV hit unchanged at 0.61, kernel usage: flash_attn_v2 (92%), fallback (8%). So batching helps reduce kernel fallback and reduces tail.
nat: interesting that KV hit didn't change — maybe the replay harness doesn't preserve exact key locality for streaming deltas. We should compare a perfect replay (no delta rewriting) to the streaming delta replay.
emily: proposal for apples-to-apples: 1) identical request arrival times, 2) identical token sequences presented to model (for streaming vs non-streaming, streaming still sends same final messages but broken into chunks; ensure the runtime reconstructs equivalent inputs), 3) same runtime config, 4) capture kernel selector logs + batching histograms + KV stats.
alex: yes — next step: create a 'packed' replay where streaming client sends all tokens at once to the runtime (simulate a non-streaming payload) but with streaming endpoints. that'll isolate client-side chunk overhead vs runtime batching.
lucas: also instrument counts: number of kernel launches, average tokens per kernel, average memory copies, NVTX marks — that'll tell us why fallback happens.
henry: FYI, I saw a perf regression from last week where a fallback path mis-evaluated sequence length because of an off-by-one in the token counter; that only showed up with chunked inputs. Could be related.
maria: let's add a short test matrix and own responsibilities:
- alex: run packed-streaming vs normal streaming (same runtime config) and attach profiler
- emily: run controlled batch_wait sweep [1,2,5,10,20] for both streaming and non-streaming
- nat: audit replay harness tokenization/merging logic for streaming deltas
- henry: add kernel selector debug logs for the next three runs
- lucas: add NVTX and kernel counters
alex: on it. starting packed-streaming now (`--stream-mode=packed`) and will drop logs in /tmp/1762501234-packed.log
replay-bot: Job 37893 started: packed-streaming
alex: quick interim: packed-streaming p99 = 240ms, KV hit=0.92, kernel: flash_attn_v2=95%.
emily: that pretty strongly points to client chunking causing the bad KV locality / more fallbacks. packed-streaming recreated the higher KV hit.
nat: confirms harness issue; we should either change replay harness to preserve token IDs across chunks or mark these tests as 'chunked-client' scenarios.
alex: for the regression ticket, I'll file: PERF-1298 "Streaming tail regression caused by client chunking + kernel selector thresholds" and include the packed vs chunked traces, profiler outputs, and recommended mitigations (raise batch.max_wait, relax kernel selector guard for small batches, improve replay harness). 
henry: also consider adding adaptive batch_wait: increase wait when many tiny chunks are observed so kernels can be used efficiently.
emily: TL;DR — not a model regress; root cause is interaction between client chunking + batching heuristics + kernel selection. Next: repro matrix + mitigation PRs.
alex: thanks everyone. I'll upload artifacts and ping here when the ticket is filed. :thumbsup:
